title: Local Feedback Loop — proto journal
content:
Purpose: brain-dump a lightweight, private local feedback loop for on-device / edge helpers that lets product teams collect high-value correction signals without breaking privacy or adding big infra cost. This is a personal scratchpad — lots of rough ideas, TODOs, and leans toward UX + telemetry rather than a formal infra design.

Problem / Context:
- We want to improve model outputs over time using real user corrections, but shipping everything to the cloud is costly and risky for PII/regulatory customers.
- Many customers run Redwood Private or Dedicated; some want a tiny on-device signal capture to inform prompt/profile generation and to surface high-signal examples back to centralized evals.
- Need to balance: usefulness (what signals are high-quality), privacy (minimize raw text leaving device), bandwidth/cost (only ship small deltas), and developer ergonomics (easy to opt-in and test).

Goals (what success looks like):
- Capture high-precision correction signals with <= 1KB median upload per event.
- 90% of collected signals must be automatically labeled (accept/reject/clarify) with minimal human triage for the first pass.
- Telemetry integration in Redwood Console showing per-customer signal rates, signal->eval mapping, and model improvement delta within 6 weeks of rollout.
- Easy SDK call: one-liner to open feedback collector on client (mobile, web, electron).

Non-goals:
- Not trying to build a full offline finetuning pipeline. This is for signal collection and prioritized sample delivery to central evals.
- Not replacing existing private dataset ingestion compliant flows for regulated enterprise customers.

High-level concept:
1) Edge-side micro-agent (JS/Swift/Kotlin) intercepts 'user correction events' — e.g., explicit thumbs-down + edit, inline correction, or flagging a hallucination.
2) Agent constructs a compact event envelope: hashed conversation id, anonymized context features (token counts, model variant id, response type), a minimal diff/patch representing the user's edit (character-level diffs or structured instruction), a local quality score (user-selected: quick slider or single tap), and a short provenance tag (UI surface id).
3) If user opts-in for richer examples, optional encrypted snippet upload (obfuscated + DP) using customer KMS or ephemeral key. Otherwise default to metadata-only.
4) Device queues events, aggregates, and uploads according to policy (on WiFi, size cap per day, or on explicit user action).
5) Central pipeline ingests compressed events, runs auto-label heuristics (edit distance threshold, instruction pattern detection, model-assertion mismatch), and heuristically assigns signal types. High-confidence signals are routed to an auto-import eval set and surfaced in Console as 'candidate corrections'.

Sketch: event envelope (informal)
- ts=UTC ISO
- device_id_hashed=H(device_uuid + salt)
- conv_len=42 tokens (approx)
- model_version=redwood/curie-v2-8bit
- signal_type=edit | rerender_request | hallucination_flag
- quality=low|medium|high (user or UI-derive)
- delta_snippet: ":- replace 'Paris' with 'Porto'" OR small json patch
- upload_mode=metadata_only | encrypted_snippet
- ui_surface=chat-thread-inline
- local_features=[avg_token_len:5.1, prompt_len:78, response_tokens:34]

Privacy knobs (mandatory):
- Default: metadata_only. Explicit consent required for snippet uploads.
- On-device redaction: detect emails/SSNs/phones using existing redaction lib -> mask before packaging.
- Add local differential privacy (DP) noise to token counts and other numeric features before upload. DP parameters configurable per-tenant.
- For enterprise Private installs: option to keep event material entirely in-customer buckets (S3) and only send signal hashes to Redwood control plane.

Auto-label heuristics (first pass):
- If edit distance / token difference > X and user quality==high -> label as 'correction' with confidence 0.9.
- If user flags hallucination and response contained named entity changes -> 'hallucination' confidence 0.8.
- If user immediately re-requests (retry) without edit -> 'temperature/hyperparam' signal.
- Unknown/ambiguous -> route to sampling queue for human triage (small %).

Developer-facing SDK API (sketch):
- RedwoodFeedback.createEvent({convId, model, uiSurface, eventType, userEdit, quality, consent}) -> returns local event ID
- RedwoodFeedback.enqueueAndUpload({policy: 'wifi-only', maxDailyBytes: 10240})
- RedwoodFeedback.setRedactionRules(rules)
- Example one-liner to open feedback modal (web): redwood.feedback.open({convId, type:'edit'})

Console UX ideas (ops):
- New console panel: 'Local Signals' with filters: tenant, model_version, signal_type, upload_mode, week-over-week signal rate.
- 'Candidate corrections' table with preview (if snippet allowed) and auto-label confidence + source percentage (how many similar corrections from different users).
- Ability to 'promote' candidate -> push to eval set or request anonymized snippet for human review.

Signal flow / infra notes:
- Edge queue -> lightweight edge-sync worker -> S3 or customer bucket -> Redwood ingestion lambda -> kafka topic -> auto-label microservice -> eval import pipeline.
- Need encrypted in-transit and at-rest; support for BYOK (customer KMS) for snippet bodies.

Open questions / risks (notes to self):
- How to avoid spam / adversarial edits? (rate-limiting per device, anomaly detection).
- Is metadata-only actually useful enough? Need experiments on signal precision.
- Legal: what counts as "user consent" across EU/UK/US? Add per-region consent flows in SDK.
- Storage/retention policy: keep raw snippets only for X days. For customers that opt-in to long-term retention, require contract.
- Can we derive meaningful features that correlate with model improvement without raw text? e.g., pattern of edits, syntactic diff size, tokens changed. Need offline experiments.

Immediate experiments (MVP):
- Build web+android minimal SDK variant that captures: conv id, model, event type, delta token counts, user-chosen quality, and optional snippet (opt-in).
- Roll to 3 internal teams (Console, Docs assistant, and a customer beta) for 2 weeks. Measure: signal throughput, % opt-in snippet, proportion auto-labeled as high-confidence, and bandwidth per device.
- Evaluate whether metadata-only signals correlate with manual labeling improvement in a held-out eval set.

Metrics to track:
- signals_per_user_day
- pct_snippet_opt_in
- avg_bytes_per_event
- auto_label_precision (compared to human triage)
- candidate_promotion_rate -> eval imports -> model delta metric (downstream; longer horizon)

Next steps / TODO (personal):
- [ ] Draft a short internal RFC for infra & data retention (link to Confluence).
- [ ] Spike a simple web SDK prototype + UI modal (2d).
- [ ] Run synthetic test dataset to validate auto-label heuristics (Evan?).
- [ ] Write a small console mockup (Figma: request from design).
- [ ] Check legal & privacy with compliance team re: DP defaults and EEA consent model.

Notes to self / style guide ideas:
- Keep default opt-out for snippet uploads; make opt-in clear and reversible.
- Prefer structured diffs (instruction-like) to raw freeform when possible — easier to auto-label.
- Build telemetry so teams can quickly see whether signals are improving eval performance — otherwise adoption will stall.

Related reading / links (personal):
- Quick sketch of DP noise schedule (local vs central) — see CONFLUENCE-2432
- Prior notes: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-sync-proto issues for offline queueing

Rough parking-lot of UX micro-ideas:
- 'Correct and teach' checkbox — if user chooses, ask 1 extra micro-question to surface intent (e.g., 'was correction factual or preference?').
- Short nudge: "Would you like to show this example to help improve the assistant?" with clear privacy blurb.
- Moderation gate: for snippet opt-in, run local profanity/name redaction before upload.

End of brain-dump — keep this a living scratch file. Will iterate into a short PRD if MVP results look promising.

-- Lina M.  (notes)
